messages:
Marta (Docs): heads-up: nightly linkcheck flagged a broken fragment on /how-to/observability -> #ingestion-rate-limit
Lint-Bot: LINKCHECK: Broken fragment -> /how-to/observability#ingestion-rate-limit (404)
Marta (Docs): the heading in observability.md is `### Ingestion rate / limit` (slash in heading) — slugify seems to replace '/' with nothing now, older slugs used a hyphen
Theo (DevEx): interesting. the new slug rules collapse punctuation differently across environments (ci vs local). could be hyphen vs empty. annoyingly external links from customers hit the old hyphenated anchor
Jules (Tech Writer): quick strategy: add an explicit HTML id on the heading AND add a tiny static redirect fragment in our netlify/_redirects or docusaurus redirects so both versions work
Ravi (Eng): patch I'll push: 
```md
### Ingestion rate / limit {#ingestion-rate-limit}
```
Ravi (Eng): and a redirect example (Netlify-style):
```text
/guide/how-to/observability#ingestion-rate-limit    /guide/how-to/observability#ingestionratelimit  301!
```
Marta (Docs): can we also add a short note in docs/contrib/slug-guidelines.md recommending avoiding slashes in headings and using explicit ids for customer-facing anchors?
Theo (DevEx): yes. I'll update the CI linkcheck to canonicalize slugs according to our chosen slugify mode and warn (not fail) on mismatches for a week while we roll redirects out
Ravi (Eng): PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/3339 (adds id + redirect + ci tweak)
Lint-Bot: PR 3339 | checks started
Jules (Tech Writer): I'll run a grep for headings with '/', '&', and ':' and file small PRs for obvious ones. helps reduce future redirects
Marta (Docs): thanks all — once CI green i'll merge and deploy. leaves: audit the top 50 inbound fragment URLs next sprint
